subtitle: Lesson 4 · Noise Models in Quantum Systems

steps.label: Decoherence error doesn't care if a gate is running
steps.sub: It only cares how much time has passed since the qubit was clean

steps.label: Gate error comes from the imperfection of the operation itself
steps.sub: A miscalibrated pulse amplitude, or a mis-shaped control pulse

steps.label: Crosstalk: a pulse for one qubit bleeds into a neighbor
steps.sub: Another source of gate error, independent of duration

steps.label: A given gate type carries roughly the same error per use
steps.sub: Largely independent of whether it takes 20 ns or 200 ns

steps.label: Decoherence (idle) error scales with elapsed time
steps.sub: Longer circuits or more idle waits grow it, exponentially

steps.label: Gate error scales with number of gate operations
steps.sub: More gates adds that many fixed-size error contributions

steps.label: At short gate times, gate error can dominate
steps.sub: A ~1e-3 gate-error floor vs. a 20 ns gate's ~2e-4 decoherence

steps.label: At longer gate times, decoherence catches up
steps.sub: Shrinking gate duration alone won't beat a fixed gate-error floor

eyebrow: Lesson 1's table, re-read against a ~1e-3 gate-error floor
code:
t = 20 ns   -> decoherence ~= 1.9998e-4   (gate error ~1e-3 dominates)

steps.label: Compilers and QEC engineers track both numbers per platform
steps.sub: The per-gate error rate, and T1/T2 — never just one

steps.label: Reducing total error means attacking whichever source dominates
steps.sub: Not trading one off blindly against the other

steps.label: Error-correcting codes tolerate a combined budget from both
steps.sub: Built in the chapters ahead, not just one source
